answer: Cross-epoch behavioural consistency rule: each identity’s action mix (counterparties, timing, value bands) is hashed into an epoch fingerprint and compared to its prior history via a similarity threshold. A copper-weight penalty applies when divergence exceeds tolerance, decaying reputation. Every extra sybil must then maintain a persistent behavioural thread across epochs, not just pass one-time checks. Divergent accounts also trigger a whisper-level review queue. Attacker cost: sustained per-identity mimicry of organic history, roughly linear in the number of identities.
